existing_definition: A live-event and corporate AV production role responsible for preparing, cueing, and playing back on-screen presentation content — slide decks, video clips, lower-thirds, and graphics — during conferences, keynotes, and corporate shows. Working from a playback system (such as PowerPoint/Keynote, ProPresenter, or a dedicated media server) and taking cues from the show caller, the presentation engineer makes sure the correct content reaches the projectors or LED walls on time and error-free. Also known as a presentation operator, graphics/screens operator, or "PowerPoint" operator.

An audio production role responsible for the design, deployment, alignment, and ongoing management of a sound-reinforcement system — specifying and rigging the loudspeakers and amplifiers, distributing signal and power, and tuning the PA for even coverage, correct level, and consistent tonal balance, typically using measurement software such as Smaart. On tours and large installations the systems manager sets up and maintains the rig so the front-of-house engineer can mix on a known, optimized system; the role is closely related to — and often used interchangeably with — systems engineer or system tech.
